** TODO Call Mum
   SCHEDULED: <2026-09-29 Tue ++2w>
   :PROPERTIES:
   :STYLE:    habit
   :END:
   :LOGBOOK:
   - State "DONE"       from "TODO"       [2026-09-21 Mon 19:20]
   - State "DONE"       from "TODO"       [2026-09-08 Tue 19:35]
   - State "DONE"       from "TODO"       [2026-08-25 Tue 20:01]
   :END:
   No slack half, so the interval itself is the cadence: 14 days.
   ++2w counts forward from the old date until it is strictly in the future, so
   ticking this off late does not put the next one in the past.
   HabitStreak() == 3.

** TODO Empty the dehumidifier
   SCHEDULED: <2026-09-21 Mon +2d>
   :PROPERTIES:
   :STYLE:    habit
   :LAST_REPEAT: [2026-09-21 Mon 12:00]
   :END:
   :LOGBOOK:
   - State "DONE"       from "TODO"       [2026-09-21 Mon 12:00]
   - State "DONE"       from "TODO"       [2026-09-19 Sat 12:14]
   :END:
   A bare + repeater: counts from the old date and may land in the past, so this
   one stays overdue until it is caught up. Contrast with .+2d above.
   HabitStreak() == 0, MissedHabit() == true - eight days against two of slack.

** TODO Back up the laptop
   SCHEDULED: <2026-09-26 Sat .+1w/9d>
   :PROPERTIES:
   :STYLE:    habit
   :LOG_INTO_DRAWER: BACKUPS
   :END:
   :BACKUPS:
   - State "DONE"       from "TODO"       [2026-09-19 Sat 14:00]
   - State "DONE"       from "TODO"       [2026-09-12 Sat 14:20]
   :END:
   An edge case worth knowing about: the completion reader asks the *file* which
   drawer the log goes in, not the heading, so a heading-level :LOG_INTO_DRAWER:
   leaves this habit with no history at all as far as the graph is concerned.
   HabitStreak() == 0 today, and MissedHabit() == true, from a habit that has in
   fact been kept.

** TODO Water the tomatoes
   SCHEDULED: <2026-09-29 Tue>
   :PROPERTIES:
   :STYLE:    habit
   :END:
   Marked a habit but with nothing repeating about its schedule, so there is no
   cadence to judge: slack is 0, MissedHabit() == false whatever happens, and a
   streak is just however many completions there have ever been (0 here).

* Repeating tasks that are not habits
  These are the contrast cases - IsHabit() must be false for all of them even
  though two of them repeat and one has a logbook full of completions.

** TODO Both planning keywords on one line
   DEADLINE: <2026-10-06 Tue> SCHEDULED: <2026-09-30 Wed .+2d>
   :PROPERTIES:
   :STYLE:    habit
   :END:
   Org keeps all of a heading's planning on one line and writes them in this
   order whenever a heading has both. A habit whose deadline gets dropped on the
   way in is the bug this one is here to catch.
